critical.issue: Returns 500 with TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'datetime.datetime' and 'str' at routes/listings.py:489 in `listings.sort(key=_sort_key, reverse=reverse)`. Pre-existing data has mixed datetime/string types in the sort key. Affects every anonymous and authenticated call to /api/listings (no query params). Independent of Feature Patch v9 but blocks marketplace listing.

rca of the issue: GET /api/listings 500 — routes/listings.py:489 calls `listings.sort(key=_sort_key, reverse=reverse)` over heterogeneous documents where _sort_key sometimes returns a datetime (newly created listings) and sometimes a string (legacy or freshly seeded docs with serialized dates). Python 3 disallows '<' between datetime and str. Reproduction: `curl $URL/api/listings`. Mitigation: in _sort_key, coerce to ISO-string or default to `datetime.min.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)` when value is not a datetime; or run a one-time migration to normalize the field type in MongoDB. Not introduced by Feature Patch v9 — but my seeding of TEST_V9_* docs with native datetime values may have made the type mix detectable on the first page of listings sorted by recency.
